source.title: Wasserstein Adversarial Regularization (WAR) on label noise
source.authors: B. Damodaran; Kilian Fatras; Sylvain Lobry; Rémi Flamary; D. Tuia; N. Courty

page_placements.theme: Held-out degradation without an established interpolation result
Selecting and correcting supervision can improve noisy-label performance

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how test accuracy changes under simulated class-dependent label noise, a related measure of V4; it does not measure training error or test fully random labels.
record.gate_note: Tests label-noise robustness on image benchmarks, but does not report training error, completely random labels, or 100% corruption. It does not test V1–V3, V5, or V6. Rows report benchmark test accuracies under simulated asymmetric noise; results cited from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study motivates a noise-robust training method using networks' memorization ability, but reports test performance rather than fitting noisy training labels. Its asymmetric-noise accuracy comparisons do not establish memorization, perfect training fit, or the real-label-versus-noise learning order.
record.authors_conclusion: The record faithfully paraphrases the authors' conclusion: WAR improves noisy-label benchmark performance and works on real-world classification and segmentation tasks. Their broad superiority statement has exceptions in the tables; for example, WAR has higher average F1 but lower overall segmentation accuracy than Bootsoft.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates Wasserstein Adversarial Regularization for class-dependent label noise; it does not reproduce the original random-label experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, noise rate, and noise structure differ across experiments; the benchmark simulations use asymmetric class-dependent noise.

fits_no_version.finding: CCE test accuracy decreases across 0%, 20%, and 40% asymmetric noise: 94.69→89.02→78.85% on Fashion-MNIST, 91.76→85.26→76.23% on CIFAR-10, and 68.60→58.81→42.45% on CIFAR-100.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Standard cross-entropy classifiers lose test accuracy as class-dependent label corruption increases over the tested range.

fits_no_version.finding: At 40% asymmetric noise, WARw2v achieves 90.41%, 84.76%, and 58.86% test accuracy, exceeding CCE's 78.85%, 76.23%, and 42.45%, respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wasserstein adversarial regularization improves test accuracy under the tested asymmetric label-noise conditions.

record.problems: The benchmark evidence uses only asymmetric noise at 0%, 20%, and 40%; the reported tables give test accuracy but no training error or fit-to-label measure. Thus these results cannot establish perfect training fit or chance test error under random labeling.
record.rows_left_out: None of the extracted benchmark test-accuracy rows were left out. Other reported results concern other tasks, architectures, or methods and do not add direct evidence on the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged training hyperparameters.
Time to fit random versus real labels and convergence speed as corruption increases. Reported timing compares methods, not label conditions.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training fit while random corruption increases through complete corruption, and the resulting joint memorization/generalization pattern. Only asymmetric-noise test performance at 0%, 20%, and 40% is reported.
Whether weight decay, dropout, and augmentation prevent random-label fitting, and whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
Separate learning trajectories for real patterns and noisy labels. The appendix's early-overfitting observation does not report these trajectories or establish their learning order.

record.verdict_notes: All extracted accuracy values match Table 1. Remove the V4 limits_scope verdict: missing training-fit measurements and untested corruption conditions are evidence gaps, not demonstrated failures of V4. The toy decision-boundary illustration and appendix observation do not establish a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: No completely random labeling or training-error results.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed across corruption levels.
No shuffled-pixel or Gaussian-noise input experiments.

The paper reports test accuracy for asymmetric label noise at 0%, 20%, and 40%; it does not report training error, perfect training fit, symmetric random labels, or a sweep through complete corruption.
No experiments on whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation prevent fitting random labels or affect true-label generalization after their removal.

relation.reason: The method addresses noisy-label overfitting, but the reported asymmetric-noise accuracies do not test any claim version. The appendix's qualitative early-overfitting observation does not establish V6's comparative learning order.

tranche.reason: The study uses memorization and overfitting as motivation for a mitigation method, reporting comparative test performance without measuring random-label training fit or real-versus-noisy-label learning order.

source_check.notes: Table 1 reports means and standard deviations averaged over the last 10 epochs of three runs. The supplied text is arXiv v3 dated 29 June 2021, although the record gives 2019.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 at 0%, 20%, and 40% simulated asymmetric noise
reader_labels.reason: Test accuracy declines with noise in these settings, but the study does not report training fit, use fully random labels, or test complete corruption (R1–R18).
